findings.title: Extreme State Complexity in Admin Users Page
findings.description: admin/users/page.tsx has 23 useState calls across 787 lines of code. This creates a cognitive overload and makes the component difficult to maintain, test, and debug. The page manages two separate tabs (teachers and students) with duplicate state management for each.
findings.recommendation: Refactor using provided custom hooks: useCrudState, useFormState, useFilterState. Create separate hooks for teacher and student state management. Target: reduce to 5-6 useState calls.
findings.whyItMatters: High state complexity increases bug risk, makes refactoring difficult, and slows down feature development. Hard to test. Performance suffers from unnecessary re-renders.

findings.title: Extreme State Complexity in Admin Settings Page
findings.description: admin/settings/page.tsx has 19 useState calls across 701 lines, consolidating 3 separate admin features (platform settings, content moderation, system monitoring) into one mega-component. This violates separation of concerns.
findings.recommendation: Split into 3 separate pages or create a page wrapper component with lazy-loaded accordion content. Use useSettings() hook for platform settings, create useModeration() and useMonitoring() hooks.
findings.whyItMatters: Mega-components are unmaintainable, hard to test, and cause performance issues. Violates single responsibility principle. Makes it difficult to add new admin features.

findings.title: Duplicated Dropdown Component Logic
findings.description: MultiSelect and SingleSelect dropdown components are defined inline in admin/users/page.tsx (lines 52-147) instead of being reusable UI components in /components/ui/. This code duplication violates DRY principle.
findings.recommendation: Extract MultiSelect and SingleSelect to /components/ui/ as reusable components. Add proper TypeScript interfaces. Use across all pages that need multi-select or single-select dropdowns.
findings.whyItMatters: Duplication makes maintenance harder. Bug fixes must be applied in multiple places. Increases bundle size. Makes testing inconsistent.

findings.title: Missing Keyboard Navigation on Dropdown Components
findings.description: Custom MultiSelect and SingleSelect dropdown components don't support keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Enter, Escape). Users cannot navigate or interact with these critical form elements using keyboard only.
findings.recommendation: Implement keyboard event handlers: Arrow Up/Down for navigation, Enter to select, Escape to close. Set tabIndex appropriately. Test with screen readers.
findings.whyItMatters: WCAG 2.1 Level A violation. Excludes users with motor disabilities. Critical for accessibility compliance. Required by law in many jurisdictions.

findings.title: Minimal ARIA Attributes in Entire Codebase
findings.description: Only 1 aria-label found in entire codebase (dialog close button). Missing: aria-labels on dropdowns, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-live regions for dynamic content, role attributes on custom components.
findings.recommendation: Add ARIA attributes to all interactive elements: buttons, forms, dropdowns, modals. Use aria-label for icon-only buttons, aria-expanded for toggles, aria-live for notifications. Run automated accessibility testing.
findings.whyItMatters: WCAG 2.1 Level A violation. Screen reader users cannot understand component purpose or state. Makes app unusable for blind/visually impaired users.

findings.title: No Semantic HTML Structure in Custom Dropdowns
findings.description: MultiSelect and SingleSelect use <div>, <button>, and <input> without semantic structure. Should use <select>, <option>, or ARIA combobox pattern. Current implementation breaks native accessibility features.
findings.recommendation: Use native <select> with optgroup for grouped options, or implement ARIA combobox pattern with proper role, aria-expanded, aria-controls attributes.
findings.whyItMatters: Screen readers cannot announce available options. Users miss context about what element is for. Violates WCAG 2.1 criterion 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value).

findings.title: Missing Form Label Associations
findings.description: Input components and form fields don't have proper <label> associations. Input labels are rendered but not connected to inputs via htmlFor attribute.
findings.recommendation: Add htmlFor={id} to all labels, generate unique IDs for form inputs. Test with screen readers to ensure labels are announced.
findings.whyItMatters: WCAG 2.1 Level A violation. Screen reader users can't understand what each input is for. Reduces usability for all users.

findings.title: Focus Management Issues in Modals and Forms
findings.description: Dialog and form components don't manage focus: no initial focus on open, no focus trap in modals, no focus restoration after close. Users can tab to off-screen elements.
findings.recommendation: Implement focus trap using useRef and useEffect. Auto-focus first input on dialog open. Restore focus to trigger element on close. Use aria-modal on dialog.
findings.whyItMatters: WCAG 2.1 Level A violation. Users with keyboard navigation lose context when focus disappears. Confusing UX even for mouse users.

findings.title: No Color Contrast Validation
findings.description: Design system uses text-xs (12px) with secondary ink color (#6b6460) on light background. Contrast ratio may not meet WCAG AA standards (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text).
findings.recommendation: Run automated contrast testing with tools like WebAIM Contrast Checker. Ensure all text meets minimum 4.5:1 ratio. Increase font size for secondary text or darken color.
findings.whyItMatters: WCAG 2.1 Level AA violation. Users with low vision or color blindness can't read content. Legal liability in many jurisdictions.

findings.title: No Error Boundaries Implemented
findings.description: Codebase has zero error boundaries. If any component throws an error, entire page crashes. No graceful error handling or recovery.
findings.recommendation: Create error boundary component in /components/ui/. Wrap each role dashboard (admin, teacher, student) with error boundary. Add error UI with recovery options.
findings.whyItMatters: Production app crashes from minor component errors. Users lose all unsaved work. Bad UX and reputation damage.

findings.title: No Lazy Loading or Code Splitting
findings.description: No dynamic imports, no React.lazy, no Next.js route-based code splitting. All 27 page components loaded at once. No lazy loading of UI components.
findings.recommendation: Use React.lazy() for heavy components (RichEditor, Charts). Use Next.js dynamic imports for admin/moderation, admin/monitoring. Implement route-based code splitting.
findings.whyItMatters: Initial bundle load is unnecessarily large. Users wait longer for first paint. Performance suffers on slow networks. Core Web Vitals impacted.

findings.title: No Render Optimization in List Components
findings.description: List components that render 100+ items have no useMemo or useCallback optimization. Teachers/students/materials lists re-render on every parent update. 139 getFullList/getList calls without pagination.
findings.recommendation: Use useMemo for list filtering/sorting. useCallback for event handlers. Implement pagination for lists >50 items. Add React.memo to list item components.
findings.whyItMatters: Unnecessary re-renders cause jank/lag. Users notice slow interactions. Mobile performance severely impacted. Battery drain on devices.

findings.title: Debug Console.error Statements in Production Code
findings.description: Multiple console.error statements remain in production code (teacher/sections, materials, homework, quizzes). These should be properly logged or removed.
findings.recommendation: Replace console.error with proper error handling using dialog context or error boundary. Or use environment-based logging for dev-only output.
findings.whyItMatters: Errors not properly reported to user. Makes debugging harder. Clutters browser console. Unprofessional appearance.

findings.title: Mega-Component Page Sizes
findings.description: Several pages exceed 700+ lines: users (787), settings (701), assessments (781), subjects_exams (699). These should be split into smaller, testable components.
findings.recommendation: Extract sub-components to separate files. Use compound components pattern. Break into smaller, focused components. Target: 200-300 lines per page.
findings.whyItMatters: Harder to maintain, harder to test, harder to understand. Performance suffers. Onboarding new developers takes longer.

findings.title: Prop Drilling Through Multiple Levels
findings.description: Multi-level component hierarchies pass props down through many levels instead of using context. Makes refactoring dangerous and prop changes affect many files.
findings.recommendation: Create domain-specific context providers: TeachersContext, StudentsContext, QuizzesContext. Move local state to context, avoid prop drilling.
findings.whyItMatters: Adding new props requires changing intermediate components. Violates separation of concerns. Makes codebase fragile.

findings.title: No State Normalization
findings.description: Data structures are nested and denormalized. Teachers have full sections array, materials have expanded teacher objects. Makes updates and queries complex.
findings.recommendation: Normalize data structures: store IDs only, use separate lookup maps. Create selectors to derive needed data. Use libraries like normalizr if needed.
findings.whyItMatters: Hard to update nested data. Leads to bugs when updating specific fields. Makes caching and memoization harder.

findings.title: Mixed Use of Logical and Physical CSS Properties
findings.description: Some components use logical properties (ms-, ps-, border-s) correctly, but others still use physical properties (border-l, ml-, pl-). Inconsistent RTL support across codebase.
findings.recommendation: Audit all CSS properties, replace physical (l, r, left, right) with logical (s, e, inline-start, inline-end). Use consistent pattern across codebase.
findings.whyItMatters: RTL layouts break in Arabic mode. Creates poor UX for Arabic-speaking users. Undermines Arabic-first design principle.

findings.title: Custom Dropdowns Don't Account for RTL Flow
findings.description: MultiSelect and SingleSelect absolute positioning assumes LTR layout. Dropdown may appear off-screen or in wrong position in RTL mode.
findings.recommendation: Use logical positioning properties or calculate position based on current dir. Test in both Arabic and English modes in desktop and mobile.
findings.whyItMatters: Dropdowns unusable in RTL mode. Critical UX bug for Arabic users. Violates Arabic-first design principle.

findings.title: 104+ Inline Classname Strings with Hardcoded CSS Variables
findings.description: Pages use long inline className strings with CSS variables instead of reusable utility classes or CSS modules. Makes design system hard to maintain and enforce.
findings.recommendation: Create reusable Tailwind utility classes or extract common patterns into CSS modules. Establish design system guidelines. Create style registry.
findings.whyItMatters: Design tokens can't be enforced. Visual inconsistencies emerge. Hard to make global style changes. Clutters code.

findings.title: Inconsistent Spacing Implementation
findings.description: Spacing varies: some components use px-3 py-2, others px-4 py-2.5. No consistent pattern for padding/margins. Makes layout unpredictable.
findings.recommendation: Define spacing scale in design system: xs (8px), sm (12px), md (16px), lg (24px), xl (32px). Create utility components that enforce spacing.
findings.whyItMatters: Layout feels inconsistent and amateurish. Harder to maintain visual harmony. Makes responsive design harder.

findings.title: No Design Token Documentation or Validation
findings.description: Design tokens exist in globals.css but no documentation of intended usage, no TypeScript types, no validation that components follow system.
findings.recommendation: Create design-tokens.ts with TypeScript definitions. Document each token's purpose. Create Storybook stories showing correct usage. Add linting rules.
findings.whyItMatters: New developers don't know how to use design system. Violations go unnoticed. Makes design system effectively invisible.

findings.title: 34 'any' Type Usages Indicating Type Safety Issues
findings.description: Multiple 'any' types in components, particularly in settings page for expanded data objects. Reduces type safety and defeats purpose of TypeScript.
findings.recommendation: Define proper interfaces for all data structures. Use strict TypeScript settings. Replace any with specific types. Use discriminated unions for expand data.
findings.whyItMatters: Type safety is lost. IDE autocomplete doesn't work. Bugs not caught at compile time. Harder to maintain.

findings.title: Missing Type Exports from Utility Modules
findings.description: Types defined in pages are not exported from /lib/ modules. Duplicate type definitions across components. Makes type sharing hard.
findings.recommendation: Create /lib/types.ts with all shared types. Export from barrel index. Import where needed. Use 'as const' for immutable types.
findings.whyItMatters: Code duplication. Type inconsistencies. Single source of truth violated.

findings.title: Custom Hooks Defined but Not Adopted in All Pages
findings.description: Custom hooks exist in /lib/hooks/ (useCrudState, useFormState, useFilterState, useTabState) but many pages still use 10+ individual useState calls instead.
findings.recommendation: Migrate old pages to use custom hooks. Update documentation on when to use each hook. Add hook usage examples to Storybook.
findings.whyItMatters: Inconsistent patterns across codebase. New developers don't know about hooks. Code is harder to test and maintain.

findings.title: No Barrel Exports for UI Components
findings.description: UI components in /components/ui/ don't have barrel export (index.ts). Each import requires full path. Makes refactoring harder.
findings.recommendation: Create index.ts that exports all UI components. Update imports to use @/components/ui. Makes refactoring easier.
findings.whyItMatters: Harder to move files. More verbose imports. Inconsistent import patterns.

findings.title: No Route-Level Error Handling
findings.description: No error.tsx or not-found.tsx at route levels. 404 errors and route failures aren't handled gracefully.
findings.recommendation: Create error.tsx and not-found.tsx in key route segments. Implement Next.js 13+ error handling. Provide recovery options.
findings.whyItMatters: Users see blank pages or confusing errors. Bad UX. Makes debugging harder.

findings.title: No Loading States for Slow Routes
findings.description: No loading.tsx components at route levels. Data-heavy pages like admin/settings may take time to load but no feedback to user.
findings.recommendation: Create loading.tsx with skeleton screens. Use Suspense boundaries. Implement streaming for large data loads.
findings.whyItMatters: Users don't know if page is loading or frozen. Reduces perceived performance.

findings.title: All Data Fetching in useEffect Without Cleanup
findings.description: 139+ getFullList/getList calls in useEffect hooks. No AbortController for request cleanup. Can cause memory leaks and race conditions.
findings.recommendation: Implement proper cleanup in useEffect return. Use AbortController to cancel in-flight requests on unmount. Consider React Query or SWR.
findings.whyItMatters: Memory leaks accumulate over time. Race conditions can cause stale data bugs. Users on slow networks experience issues.

findings.title: No Caching or Deduplication of API Calls
findings.description: Same data fetched multiple times across pages. No caching layer. Users make redundant API calls causing server load and slow UX.
files: All pages with materials, homework, sections
findings.recommendation: Use React Query, SWR, or create custom caching layer. Cache user sections, subjects. Dedup simultaneous requests.
findings.whyItMatters: Unnecessary server load. Slower app performance. Poor UX on slow networks. Increased bandwidth costs.

findings.title: No Pagination for Large Lists
findings.description: getFullList calls fetch all records without pagination. Admin pages with 100+ teachers, 300+ students load all at once.
findings.recommendation: Implement pagination with page numbers and limit. Add virtual scrolling for lists >1000 items. Show loading states.
findings.whyItMatters: Large data loads are slow. Memory usage high. UI becomes sluggish. Bad mobile performance.

findings.title: Direct Data Access Without Validation
findings.description: Code assumes PocketBase API rules are enforced. No client-side validation that user has permission to access data.
findings.recommendation: Add client-side permission checks before rendering. Validate user role matches expected data. Handle 403 responses.
findings.whyItMatters: If API rules are misconfigured, users see data they shouldn't. Bad UX when permissions fail. Security liability.

findings.title: No Input Sanitization in Forms
findings.description: Form inputs go directly into API calls without sanitization. Rich editor uses DOMPurify but other inputs don't.
findings.recommendation: Sanitize all user inputs. Use validation libraries. Escape HTML in display contexts. Add Content Security Policy headers.
findings.whyItMatters: Potential XSS attacks if data is displayed unsanitized. Malicious users could inject scripts.

findings.title: No Testing Infrastructure or Test Files
findings.description: Zero test files found. No Jest config, no React Testing Library setup. No unit, integration, or E2E tests.
findings.recommendation: Set up Jest + React Testing Library. Write unit tests for hooks and components. Add E2E tests with Playwright. Target >70% coverage.
findings.whyItMatters: No safety net for refactoring. Bugs found in production. Harder to maintain. Slower development velocity.

findings.title: No Storybook or Component Documentation
findings.description: No Storybook setup. UI components not documented or showcased. No design system reference. New developers don't know what components exist.
findings.recommendation: Set up Storybook. Create stories for each UI component. Show variants and states. Add accessibility tests.
findings.whyItMatters: Developers don't know what components are available. Lead to duplication. Inconsistent UI usage.

findings.title: No Separation Between Admin/Teacher/Student Feature Contexts
findings.description: No separate contexts for admin, teacher, student feature states. All use same generic contexts. Makes adding role-specific features harder.
findings.recommendation: Create role-specific contexts: AdminContext, TeacherContext, StudentContext. Share common functionality through utility functions.
findings.whyItMatters: Harder to add role-specific features. State management becomes complex. Makes codebase less maintainable.

findings.title: No Query Parameter Handling for Filtering/Sorting
findings.description: List pages don't use query parameters for filters, sorting, pagination. Refreshing page loses filter state. Can't share filtered views via URL.
findings.recommendation: Sync filters, sort, pagination to URL query params. Use next/router to read params on mount. Implement with useQueryState or similar.
findings.whyItMatters: Can't share specific views. Refresh loses state. URL doesn't reflect page content. Bad for bookmarking and sharing.

findings.title: Components.md Plan Not Fully Implemented
findings.description: UX plan (components.md) defines best practices and recommendations but many pages still violate them. Pages with 18+ states still exist, custom hooks not adopted universally.
findings.recommendation: Use components.md as migration guide. Systematically refactor pages to meet recommendations. Add CI/CD linting to enforce state limits.
findings.whyItMatters: Planned architecture not realized. Technical debt accumulates. Defeats purpose of planning phase.

findings.title: Routing.md Plan Followed But Admin Routes Too Many
findings.description: Routing plan defines admin routes but admin has 11+ routes when plan suggested consolidation. Some routes should be nested.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate admin routes: create /dashboard/admin/academic (sections+subjects), /dashboard/admin/content (moderation+monitoring+settings), /dashboard/admin/users (teachers+students).
findings.whyItMatters: Too many routes make navigation confusing. URL structure doesn't reflect feature relationships.

findings.title: Missing Bilingual Date/Time Formatting
findings.description: Dates and times displayed using default locale. Not formatted according to Arabic/English preferences. Time zones not considered.
findings.recommendation: Use date-fns or Intl API with locale formatting. Show dates in Arabic format for Arabic locale, English format for English.
findings.whyItMatters: Dates confusing to users. 12-hour vs 24-hour format not respected. Minor i18n issue.

findings.title: No Pluralization Support
findings.description: Stats show 'X materials' without pluralization handling. Arabic needs complex pluralization rules.
findings.recommendation: Use i18next or similar for pluralization. Define plural rules for Arabic. Use formatList for multiple items.
findings.whyItMatters: Grammatically incorrect in Arabic. Minor i18n issue but affects quality perception.

findings.title: No Touch-Optimized Tap Targets
findings.description: Touch targets sometimes <44px per WCAG. Custom dropdown buttons are small. Icon buttons may be hard to tap on mobile.
findings.recommendation: Ensure all interactive elements are 44px minimum (iOS) or 48px (Android). Add padding around small buttons. Test on actual mobile devices.
findings.whyItMatters: Hard to use on mobile. Frustrating UX. Accessibility issue. Reduces mobile engagement.

findings.title: No Mobile-Specific Navigation Optimization
findings.description: Sidebar navigation good but mobile tab bar has 5 items. Bottom tab bar may have overflow issues on small screens.
findings.recommendation: Test navigation on various mobile widths. Consider hamburger menu for smaller screens. Use fixed bottom tab only for main items.
findings.whyItMatters: Mobile UX could be better. Navigation might be cluttered on small phones.

findings.title: No Image Optimization or Lazy Loading
findings.description: Public assets (logo.webp) exist but no Next.js Image component used. No responsive image sizes. No WebP format with fallbacks.
findings.recommendation: Use next/image for all images. Set sizes prop for responsive images. Use WebP with fallback. Add loading='lazy' for below-fold images.
findings.whyItMatters: Images not optimized for different screen sizes. Mobile bundle too large. Page load slower.

findings.title: No Environment-Based Logging Configuration
findings.description: console.error statements visible in all environments. No log level configuration.
findings.recommendation: Create logging utility with environment-based levels. Use dev-only logging. Consider error tracking service.
findings.whyItMatters: Production console polluted. Hard to distinguish real errors from dev logs.

suggestions: Implement comprehensive error boundaries for production stability
Adopt custom hooks universally across all pages - start with Priority 1 pages (users, settings)
Extract MultiSelect/SingleSelect to reusable components with full keyboard and ARIA support
Create barrel exports for UI components to simplify imports
Set up Jest + React Testing Library with >70% coverage target
Implement React Query or SWR for data fetching, caching, and deduplication
Add Storybook for component documentation and accessibility testing
Audit and fix all WCAG 2.1 Level A violations (aria labels, keyboard nav, focus management)
Create design system documentation with TypeScript types for all tokens
Migrate all pages from 'any' types to strict TypeScript
Add route-level error.tsx and loading.tsx for graceful error handling
Implement query parameter syncing for filters and pagination
Set up automated accessibility testing in CI/CD pipeline
Consolidate admin routes from 11 to 5-7 logical groupings
Add AbortController cleanup to all useEffect data fetching
Implement pagination and virtual scrolling for large lists (>50 items)
Replace physical CSS properties with logical ones (l→s, r→e) for full RTL support
Create role-specific context providers (AdminContext, TeacherContext, StudentContext)
Add Next.js Image optimization for all images
Set up Playwright E2E tests for critical user journeys (login, create material, submit homework)
